claims.text: The funding opportunity offers seed funding for collaborative projects.
The funding is for UK-Japan collaborative projects.
The projects can be in fields including arts, culture, humanities, science, youth, education, and sport.
The funding is for projects that deepen mutual understanding between the UK and Japan.
The funding is for projects that encourage the exchange of ideas or expertise between the UK and Japan.
The funding is for projects that develop lasting collaboration between the UK and Japan.
Awards will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000.
Awards will only exceptionally exceed £6,000.
Applicants are encouraged to seek or have secured other sources of funding.
Applications are accepted for projects in all fields.
Grant money can be used to support festivals, workshops, performances and other events that present aspects of Japan to the UK or the UK to Japan.
Grant money can be used to support exchanges between the two countries for schools, sporting groups, artists, artisans, performers, scientists and researchers.
Grant money can be used to support collaborative projects involving UK and Japanese participants that result in new and innovative outputs.
Grant money can be used to support the teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies in schools and higher education.
Grant money can be used to support academic research, visits and exchange where these push forward knowledge or involve collaboration.
Projects that show genuine collaboration between the UK and Japan are of particular interest.
Projects that result in new outputs with clear benefits for people beyond the project itself are of particular interest.
Applicants should demonstrate a realistic plan for delivering their project, with a clear budget and key dates and activities.
Applicants should explain how support from the Foundation will make a meaningful difference to the project.
Most awards are considered on a case-by-case basis.
There is no formal limit on the amount that can be applied for unless applying for PhD research or travel costs.
For very small projects, grant funds may cover the whole project.
More normally, grant funds give only partial support, with applicants demonstrating secured or planned additional funding.
For travel and subsistence in Japan for trips up to 13 days, the UK office will award up to £2,000 per person.
For travel and subsistence in Japan for trips of 14 days or more, the UK office will award up to £2,500 per person.
These travel limits are applied to projects involving up to two people.
For three or more people traveling, the UK office may award a lower overall amount to stay within the £1,500-£5,000 range.
The UK office will consider awards of up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more.
The Japan office will consider awards of up to ¥300,000 for Japanese PhD students traveling to the UK for fieldwork or research.
Grants are not made for consumables, salaries, or purchase of materials.
Grants are not made for capital projects such as building purchase, construction or maintenance.
Grants are not made for student fees or travel related to study for a qualification (excluding PhD students).
Grants are not made to support undergraduate or master’s students.
Grants are not made for retrospective activity.
Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds.
Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects.
The UK office may consider applications from individuals who can provide proof of organisational support.
Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
Applications are welcomed from previous recipients for new projects.
Applications for small grants can be submitted to both UK and Japan offices.
Projects originating in the UK should be submitted through the UK office.
Projects originating in Japan should be submitted through the Japan office.
The same project cannot be submitted to both offices.
The UK office holds three annual awards meetings.
Application deadlines for the UK office are 31 March, 15 September, and 15 December.
Decisions for UK applications submitted by 31 March are made in May.
Decisions for UK applications submitted by 15 September are made in November.
Decisions for UK applications submitted by 15 December are made in March.
All applications to the UK office must use a specific application form.
Applications from PhD students to the UK office must include a letter of support from the PhD supervisor.
Applications and enquiries for the UK office must be sent by email to grants@gbsf.org.uk.
The Japan office holds two annual awards meetings.
Application deadlines for the Japan office are 28 February and 30 September.
Decisions for Japan applications submitted by 28 February are made in April.
Decisions for Japan applications submitted by 30 September are made in November.
There is no set report format for applicants to the Japan office.
To apply to the Japan office, applicants should email tokyo@gbsf.org.uk for further details.
The UK application form should not be used for Japan applications.
Successful applicants must make a change request if substantial changes occur in their plans.
Successful applicants must acknowledge the Foundation's support in their own channels and use its logo in publicity material.
Successful applicants must contribute or collaborate on content for social media channels, the website, and annual review.
Successful applicants must submit a brief post-project report within three months of completion.
There is no prescribed final report form for applicants to the Japan Office.
